name: Corporate Account Takeover and Wire Fraud
description: Attackers take over business online-banking credentials and initiate fraudulent wires before the customer or the bank detects them.
asset: Business online banking and wire transfer rails
assumptions: A loss event is at least one fraudulent wire leaving the bank.
Recovery through the receiving bank is reflected in primary loss.
Secondary loss covers customer litigation and examiner findings.

name: Ransomware Disrupts Branch and Core Systems
description: Ransomware spreads from the corporate network toward core banking connectivity; branches fall back to manual limits while systems are rebuilt.
asset: Core banking connectivity and branch systems
assumptions: The core processor itself stays up; the outage is our connectivity and branch estate.
Manual limits cap transaction exposure during downtime.
Secondary loss covers regulatory response and customer attrition.

name: Insider Manipulates Customer Accounts
description: An employee with elevated access moves funds or alters records across customer accounts until pattern monitoring or a complaint surfaces it.
assumptions: An incident is unauthorized movement or alteration that requires restitution.
Vulnerability reflects the chance monitoring misses it past one cycle.
Secondary loss includes bonding claims and examiner scrutiny.

name: Card Data Compromise at a Processor
description: A breach at a card processor or ATM fleet exposes card data issued by the bank, driving reissuance, fraud losses, and brand assessments.
asset: Issued card portfolio and ATM fleet
threat: Attacker compromising a processor or ATM estate
assumptions: A threat event is a compromise touching our issued cards.
Primary loss covers reissuance and absorbed card fraud.
Secondary loss includes card-brand assessments and customer attrition.

name: Nonpublic Customer Data Exposure
description: A misconfigured share or third-party integration exposes nonpublic personal information, triggering GLBA notification and examiner attention.
assumptions: An exposure becomes a loss event only if NPI is actually accessible.
Primary loss covers forensics, notification, and monitoring.
Secondary loss includes examiner-driven remediation programs.
